label: Digitally Immersed & Emotionally Distressed
summary: This profile represents highly educated women who spend more than 5 hours daily online and report elevated levels of loneliness, depressive symptoms, and anxiety. With a UCLA-8 loneliness mean of 1.74, a PHQ-9 depression mean of 1.75, and a notably high GAD-7 anxiety mean of 2.17, these respondents consistently score above moderate thresholds across all three psychological distress dimensions. Their extensive screen time may both reflect and reinforce patterns of social isolation and emotional difficulty.
demographic_anchor: Female, graduate-level education or above, daily screen time exceeding 5 hours
behavior_markers: Extended daily screen time (more than 5 hours)
Co-occurrence of loneliness, depression, and anxiety suggesting compounded emotional distress

label: Well-Adjusted Male Graduate
summary: This profile represents respondents who report lower levels of loneliness, depressive symptoms, and anxiety symptoms compared to other groups. With UCLA-8 loneliness, PHQ-9 depression, and GAD-7 anxiety scores all well below scale midpoints, these individuals demonstrate generally positive psychological well-being across all three measured dimensions.
demographic_anchor: Male, holding a graduate degree or above, with 1–3 hours of daily screen time or online activity
behavior_markers: Reports minimal loneliness (UCLA-8 mean ≈ 0.77, near the low end of the scale)
Exhibits very low depressive symptomatology (PHQ-9 mean ≈ 0.33)
Maintains moderate and limited daily screen time (1–3 hours)
Represents a relatively large and stable subgroup (n = 150 in training split)

label: Lonely but Emotionally Resilient
summary: This profile captures respondents who report notably elevated loneliness yet maintain relatively low levels of depressive and anxiety symptoms. Despite feeling socially disconnected, they do not exhibit the affective distress typically associated with loneliness, suggesting a degree of emotional resilience or effective coping that buffers against mood and anxiety disorders.
demographic_anchor: Predominantly female, holding graduate-level education or above, with moderate daily screen/internet use of 1–3 hours
behavior_markers: Reports higher-than-average loneliness on the UCLA-8 scale (mean ≈ 1.30)
Maintains low depressive symptom severity on the PHQ-9 (mean ≈ 0.86)
Exhibits low anxiety symptom severity on the GAD-7 (mean ≈ 0.91)
Moderate digital engagement (1–3 hours daily), suggesting limited but purposeful online activity
Experiences social disconnection without corresponding deterioration in mood or anxiety
tone: Quietly isolated yet psychologically stable; reflective and self-contained rather than distressed
